question: Does God respect anyone?
summary: Genesis 4 has Yahweh preferring Abel's offering and rejecting Cain's — he respects persons. A seven-verse stack from Deuteronomy, 2 Chronicles, Acts, Romans, Galatians, Ephesians, Colossians, and 1 Peter then insists God is no respecter of persons. The Hebrew Bible shows explicit favoritism; the New Testament stack, and a few Old Testament echoes, deny it exists.

reconcile.connective: Commentators distinguish God as impartial judge — who weighs no man's outward status — from God as sovereign benefactor, who freely accepted Abel's faith over Cain's.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, lists this exact pairing — God's respect for Abel over Cain in Genesis 4 against the stack of verses (Deut 10:17; Acts 10:34; Rom 2:11; etc.) declaring God no respecter of persons — as a standing contradiction.

pd_work.note: Henry treats this exact tension at Acts 10:34, distinguishing God as sovereign benefactor (who gives favours 'arbitrarily and by sovereignty') from God as impartial judge, and ties the principle back to Genesis 4:7.

excerpts.excerpt_text: that God is no respecter of persons—Not, "I see there is no capricious favoritism with God," for Peter would never imagine such a thing; but (as the next clause shows), "I see that God has respect only to personal character and state in the acceptance of men, national and ecclesiastical distinctions being of no account."
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Defines 'no respecter of persons' as the absence of favoritism toward outward national/ecclesiastical status, not the absence of all preference — God still has respect to personal character, which is exactly the Abel-vs-Cain ground.
